clue.text: Blunder in accounts I am ill in consequence

indicators.note: a consequence is what comes out of something, so the preceding letters are worked out into a fresh order

parts.note: all fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper confesses that a mistake in the accounts has made them ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'in accounts' together as the place of the blunder; 'in' is only a joining word and the fodder is the whole run of fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscalculation is an error of reckoning, a synonym for a blunder or mistake.

parts.note: a monkey is a primate; the possessive just runs it into the next word
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: An archbishop's company is caught in dodgy deals.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate looks like a senior bishop, the obvious church reading; here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is an idiom for mischief or underhand, dishonest conduct.

definitions.note: adjective in the phrase 'a sinking feeling'

parts.note: sin is wickedness
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A wicked ruler stirs up resentment among the people.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition only works through the phrase 'a sinking feeling'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinking feeling is the idiom for a sudden sense of dread or dismay, an unpleasant emotion.

parts.note: surface reading: a skilled artist
setter's reading: a great painter of the past is called an Old Master, so 'master' is the key word

explanation.surface: A skilled artist who may be getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Masters are the great European painters before about 1800; an art master is also a school art teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of art is one expert in painting, and the most celebrated are called Old Masters.

parts.note: cher is French for dear, expensive
Roman numeral
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A herb sold overseas at a steep price of six pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chervil is a parsley-like culinary herb with a faint aniseed flavour.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small medicated sweet, a throat pastille

explanation.surface: Something as sweet as a precious gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is both a sucked tablet or sweet and the rhombus figure also called a diamond.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British private soldier

explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier boy' reads as one young recruit; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is slang for a British private, after the specimen name Thomas Atkins, and a pet form of Thomas.

parts.note: workers who are striking are said to be out
a crop is a harvest

explanation.surface: An impressive yield gathered at harvest time.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: rock that strikes out of the ground, a 'crop' that is out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is a mass of bedrock that protrudes above the soil surface, standing out conspicuously.

parts.note: surface reading: the royal family's castle in the English county of Berkshire
setter's reading: a royal family is a dynasty, called a house, named here after a Berkshire town

explanation.surface: The castle where the British royal family stay in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London; its town of Windsor gave its name to the royal dynasty in 1917.
explanation.definitionFit: The British royal family is the dynasty of Windsor, and a dynasty is called a house, the pun on residence.

parts.note: surface reading: a girl standing on, or relying on, two refusals
setter's reading: the girl whose name comes after 'No, No' in the title of a famous musical

explanation.surface: A girl perched on a pair of negatives, as if on photographic film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, No, Nanette' is a 1925 musical comedy; the heroine's name follows two noes in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of the musical is a girl, and in the show's title her name comes after two refusals.

clue.text: Russian assembly's relish about a number on the left-hand page

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped around another

parts.note: zest is keen enjoyment, relish
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
VO is short for verso, the left-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A Russian council enjoys hunting for a figure printed on a book's left page.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', joining definition to wordplay; 'on' places VO after the rest in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A zemstvo was an elected local council in tsarist Russia, a provincial assembly set up in 1864.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a girl's first name
second meaning: the botanical genus of heaths and heathers

explanation.surface: A young woman whose name is Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a girl's name too, but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is both a common feminine given name and the Latin genus name for the heather plants.

parts.note: surface reading: publishers or writers sending their work to be printed
setter's reading: the crop is crushed in a wine press

explanation.surface: Publishers whose books are sent off to the printers.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapes grown on vine plantations are taken to a wine press to be crushed for their juice.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a table game of rolling balls into holes among pins

definitions.note: an adjective phrase; the answer is a noun, a thing of no significance

explanation.surface: A pastime that matters to nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a pin-table game, and the word also means a trifle, something too slight to matter.

parts.note: surface reading: an animal belonging to a religious order of Augustinian friars
setter's reading: Saint Augustine was bishop of a North African city whose name is also a large river animal

explanation.walkthrough: Saint Augustine is known as Augustine of Hippo, after the Roman city where he was bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The short name of the hippopotamus matches the city Hippo Regius, Augustine's see, so it is his beast by name.

definitions.note: a verb phrase completing the sentence 'a jug may ...'
definitions.meaning: first meaning: what a sound jug can do with liquid
second meaning: of an argument, stand up to scrutiny

explanation.surface: A jug might be good enough to pass inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is not a definition on its own but a sentence the answer completes.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument that holds water is sound and survives testing, the idiom for standing up to scrutiny.

parts.note: south is one of the four quarters of the compass
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: Pouring a quarter of a jug down the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is an underground drain carrying waste water away.

clue.text: Was the contemptuous expression meant to sting?

parts.note: taken as written
pish is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a scornful remark was intended to wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the insect: being like a wasp means set on stinging.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means sharply irritable and spiteful, with remarks meant to hurt like an insect's sting.

clue.text: Unseen, unlooked for, . and unenvied beast?

definitions.text: Unseen, unlooked for, . and unenvied beast?

parts.words: Unseen, unlooked for, . and unenvied beast
parts.note: surface reading: some creature nobody has seen, hoped to find or wished to be
setter's reading: each word sums up a line of Gelett Burgess's comic verse about an animal of an impossible colour

explanation.surface: A mysterious animal that no one has seen, sought or envied.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgess's rhyme runs: 'I never saw a Purple Cow, I never hope to see one; But I can tell you, anyhow, I'd rather see than be one.' The stray full stop is a print blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's cow was never seen, never hoped for, and the poet would rather see one than be one.

clue.text: First part of April with a girl

indicators.note: only part of the next word is kept, so its outside letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's birthday falls early in April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First part of April' looks like a single phrase meaning A; 'First' is the definition and 'part of' trims April at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Primary means first in order or importance, as in a primary school or primary cause.

clue.text: Pink chair with eggs round it

indicators.note: round it says the second item goes around the first like a ring

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A pink armchair surrounded by eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured, a literary word for pink.

parts.note: surface reading: an implement with a cushioned handle
setter's reading: a pet's foot has soft pads, and a person used as someone else's tool shares its name

explanation.walkthrough: From the fable of the monkey that used a cat's foot to pull chestnuts from the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is a dupe used by another to do their dirty work, and a cat's foot is literally padded.

clue.text: Heresiarch is not sure to be convened

indicators.note: convened means called together into a new gathering, so the letters assemble in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The founder of a heresy doubts whether a church council will meet.
explanation.walkthrough: A heresiarch is the founder of a heresy; a council (the Council of Ephesus, 431) is just what condemned this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, gave his name to Nestorianism, condemned as heretical, making him a leading heresy founder.

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
dour means stern, grim

explanation.surface: Something gloomy gives off a smell of nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour is a smell, a near synonym for scent.

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A council member declares what they want.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no anagram word: the question mark is all that warns the letters of 'I want' must be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the advisory assembly of Anglo-Saxon kings, the council of wise men.

clue.text: Philosopher of Zion disturbed in the spring

indicators.note: in places the jumbled word inside the other piece

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of their settled positions into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker of Zion is troubled during springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The spring' suggests the season; it is a spring of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was the seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist philosopher, author of the Ethics.

clue.text: Herod in his palace can tip a slave

indicators.note: living within his palace walls suggests the name sits enclosed inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the word breaks

explanation.surface: King Herod, at home in his palace, can give a slave a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod Antipas was the son of Herod the Great who ruled Galilee in the time of Jesus.

clue.text: A long struggle to make writer try ana say Ah!

indicators.note: to make something is to build it from raw material, so the letters are put together into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author labours for ages, trying to produce the perfect satisfied sigh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ana' between the two halves of the fodder is almost certainly the scan's misreading of 'and', a plain joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thirty Years' War of 1618 to 1648 was a drawn-out European conflict, so a long struggle indeed.
